subtopics.description: Definition of linearity including superposition and homogeneity principles. Comparison with non-linear phenomena to establish why linear systems are mathematically tractable and widely used as approximations.
Everyday scenarios modeled linearly: supply-demand economics, mixing problems, structural analysis. Emphasis on identifying linear relationships in complex systems.
Survey of core topics: vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues. High-level roadmap connecting these concepts to provide orientation before detailed study.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Applications: Google PageRank and Google Maps
subtopics.description: Case studies demonstrating linear algebra's power in modern technology: PageRank as eigenvector problem, navigation algorithms in mapping services. Motivation for the course.

topics.learning_intent: Understand the fundamental concept of linearity and its distinction from non-linearity, and recognize real-world applications where linear algebra plays a critical role.

subtopics.description: Introduction to vectors as ordered n-tuples of numbers. Operations: addition, scalar multiplication. Linear combination concept: c1*v1 + c2*v2 + ... + ck*vk. Geometric visualization in 2D and 3D. Spanning interpretation.
Geometric interpretation of systems of equations as intersecting lines (2D) and planes (3D). Row picture vs. column picture representation. Understanding solution sets as geometric objects.

Row operations: swapping, scaling, adding multiples. Forward elimination to echelon form. Pivots and leading variables. Back substitution. Augmented matrices. Connection between elimination and matrix factorization.

Definition of rank as the number of pivots after elimination. Rank and linear independence relationship. Full rank, rank-deficient, and full row/column rank cases. Rank conditions for solution existence.
Row echelon form and reduced row echelon form (RREF). Procedures to obtain RREF. Identifying free and basic variables from the form. Solution writing from RREF.

Homogeneous systems (Ax = 0): always have trivial solution, non-trivial solutions when rank < n. Non-homogeneous systems (Ax = b): solution existence condition (rank(A) = rank(A|b)). Parametric solution forms.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Applications: Machine Learning, Cryptography, Color Models
subtopics.description: Practical case studies: solving normal equations in linear regression (ML); encoding/decoding messages using linear systems (cryptography); representing colors as vectors and transforming between RGB and CMYK color spaces.

topics.learning_intent: Represent and solve systems of linear equations using matrix methods, understand the geometric interpretation of solutions, and apply these techniques to practical problems in machine learning, cryptography, and color models.

subtopics.description: Axiomatic definition of vector space over R or C. Examples: R^n, polynomials, matrices, function spaces. Subspace definition and tests: closed under addition and scalar multiplication. Span as a subspace. Column space and null space as subspaces.

Span of a set of vectors. Linear combination interpretation. Linear dependence and independence: definition via trivial combination (only trivial solution = independent). Dependency relations. Spanning sets and their minimal subsets.

Basis as a linearly independent spanning set. Standard bases for R^n. Coordinates relative to a basis. Dimension as cardinality of basis. Dimension theorem for subspaces. Invariance of dimension (all bases have same size).

Linear transformations defined on vector spaces. Matrix representation of linear maps relative to bases. Domain, codomain, range. Composition of linear maps. Invertible (nonsingular) linear transformations. Isomorphisms between vector spaces.

Kernel (null space) of a linear transformation: set of vectors mapping to zero. Image (range) of a transformation. Nullity and rank defined dimensionally. Relationship between these spaces and the transformation matrix.

Statement and proof of rank-nullity theorem: dim(domain) = rank + nullity. Applications: determining if a linear map is injective or surjective from dimensions. Consequences for matrix transformations.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Similarity of Matrices and Change of Basis
subtopics.description: Similar matrices B = P^{-1}AP represent same linear transformation in different bases. Similarity invariants: determinant, trace, eigenvalues. Change of basis matrix computation. Diagonalization as a special case of change of basis.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Inner Product Spaces, Norms, and Orthogonality
subtopics.description: Inner product definition: dot product in R^n, general <u,v> = u^TAv. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Vector norms: Euclidean, taxicab, infinity norm. Orthogonal vectors: definition via zero inner product. Orthogonal complement.
prerequisites_within_course: Similarity of Matrices and Change of Basis

subtopics.description: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization procedure to produce orthonormal basis from any basis. QR decomposition connection. Applications: data smoothing via projection onto lower-dimensional subspaces, image scaling using coordinate transformations.
prerequisites_within_course: Inner Product Spaces, Norms, and Orthogonality

topics.learning_intent: Comprehend abstract vector space concepts including subspaces, basis, dimension, and linear transformations. Apply the rank-nullity theorem and use Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization for practical applications in data smoothing and image scaling.

subtopics.description: Characteristic polynomial det(A - λI). Finding eigenvalues as roots of characteristic polynomial. Cayley-Hamilton theorem: every matrix satisfies its characteristic equation. Applications: computing powers of matrices using characteristic polynomial.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors: Computation and Properties
subtopics.description: Eigenvalue-eigenvector definition: Av = λv. Finding eigenvectors for known eigenvalues. Eigenspace as null space of (A - λI). Algebraic multiplicity vs. geometric multiplicity. Linear independence of eigenvectors from distinct eigenvalues.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Geometric Interpretation of Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
subtopics.description: Eigenvectors as directions unchanged by the transformation (scaled only). Eigenvalue as scaling factor. Visualizing transformations: identifying stretching/compressing directions. Fixed directions in rotation matrices (complex eigenvalues).
prerequisites_within_course: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors: Computation and Properties

subtopics.description: Diagonalizable matrices: A = PDP^{-1} where D is diagonal. Conditions for diagonalization: sufficient condition of n distinct eigenvalues; necessary and sufficient: enough independent eigenvectors. Computing A^k via diagonalization: A^k = PD^kP^{-1}.
prerequisites_within_course: Geometric Interpretation of Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors

subtopics.description: Symmetric matrix properties: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors. Spectral theorem for symmetric matrices. Quadratic forms: x^TAx, classification as positive definite, negative definite, indefinite. Principal axis theorem. Constrained optimization with quadratic forms.

Overdetermined systems (more equations than unknowns) and approximate solutions. Normal equations: (A^TA)x = A^Tb. Geometric interpretation: projection onto column space. Applications in data fitting and machine learning regression.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Applications: Facial Recognition, Feature Extraction, Search Engines
subtopics.description: Eigenfaces: using principal eigenvectors of face image covariance for recognition. Eigenvalue-based feature importance in dimensionality reduction. PageRank revisited as eigenvector of the web link matrix with eigenvalue 1.

topics.learning_intent: Compute and interpret eigenvalues and eigenvectors for applications in facial recognition, feature extraction, and search engine algorithms. Use diagonalization for matrix powers and apply symmetric matrix properties to quadratic forms.

subtopics.description: Review of eigendecomposition for symmetric matrices: A = QΛQ^T with orthogonal Q. Properties: orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, real eigenvalues. Spectral decomposition as expansion in rank-1 projections: A = Σ λ_i * q_i * q_i^T.

SVD definition: A = UΣV^T where U and V are orthogonal, Σ is diagonal with singular values. Relationship to eigenvalues of A^TA and AA^T. Left singular vectors (columns of U) and right singular vectors (columns of V). Full vs. reduced SVD.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Rank-k Approximation and the Best Rank-k Approximation
subtopics.description: Truncated SVD with k singular values: A_k = U_k Σ_k V_k^T. Eckart-Young theorem: A_k is the best rank-k approximation in Frobenius norm. Error bound using discarded singular values. Applications in image compression and noise reduction.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Power Method for Computing Dominant Singular Values
subtopics.description: Power iteration for dominant eigenvector of A^TA. Rayleigh quotient interpretation. Convergence behavior and rate dependence on eigenvalue gap. Deflation for finding subsequent singular vectors. Practical implementation considerations.
prerequisites_within_course: Rank-k Approximation and the Best Rank-k Approximation

subtopics.subtopic_name: Applications: PCA, Data Centering, Document Ranking, Clustering
subtopics.description: Principal Component Analysis via SVD of centered data matrix. Data centering (subtracting mean) for PCA. Latent Semantic Indexing for document ranking in information retrieval. K-means clustering connection to SVD-based dimensionality reduction. Worked examples with real datasets.
prerequisites_within_course: Power Method for Computing Dominant Singular Values

topics.learning_intent: Understand SVD as a generalization of eigenvalue decomposition to non-square matrices, apply rank-k approximation for data compression, and implement the power method for computing dominant singular values in PCA and information retrieval.

subtopics.description: Modeling traffic networks as linear systems using flow conservation (Kirchhoff's current law). Solving for unknown traffic volumes at intersections. Kirchhoff's voltage law for electrical circuits. Writing and solving circuit equations for resistor networks.

Representing chemical reactions as systems of linear equations. Balancing stoichiometric coefficients by solving homogeneous systems. Identifying conservation equations from molecular composition. Worked examples including combustion and redox reactions.

Image representation as a matrix. Applying SVD and truncating to k singular values for compression. Compression ratio calculation and trade-off with reconstruction error. Implementation using Python/MATLAB with sample images. Comparison with JPEG compression principles.
prerequisites_within_course: Rank-k Approximation and the Best Rank-k Approximation

subtopics.description: Representing words as vectors in high-dimensional space using co-occurrence matrices. Dimensionality reduction via SVD (Latent Semantic Analysis). Semantic relationships encoded in vector differences. Applications in natural language processing.

Stochastic matrices and Markov chains. Power method for stationary distribution. PageRank as application: web graph as Markov matrix, damping factor, solving for stationary distribution. Sensitivity analysis and interpretation of rankings.
prerequisites_within_course: Power Method for Computing Dominant Singular Values

subtopics.subtopic_name: Bias in Data and Geometric Interpretations
subtopics.description: How data representation choices introduce bias. Geometric view: alignment of data with principal components. Analyzing high-dimensional representations for discriminatory patterns. Case studies in algorithmic bias and fairness considerations.
prerequisites_within_course: Applications: PCA, Data Centering, Document Ranking, Clustering

subtopics.description: Matrix games and payoff matrices in game theory. Solving two-player zero-sum games using linear algebra (dominance, saddle points). Chess move matrices and move prediction. Term-document matrices and TF-IDF ranking in search engines.

subtopics.subtopic_name: Special Applications: Chessboard Moves and Genetics Modeling
subtopics.description: Chessboard coverage problems as linear independence and spanning. Knight's tour as matrix exponentiation problem. Leslie matrices in population genetics for age-structured populations. Predator-prey models using linear recurrence relations.

topics.learning_intent: Solve practical engineering and scientific problems using linear algebra techniques including traffic flow analysis, circuit analysis, chemical equation balancing, and Markov chain modeling for PageRank. Implement compression algorithms using SVD and understand bias implications in data representations.

syllabus.coverage_summary: This undergraduate Linear Algebra course provides a comprehensive treatment of fundamental concepts and their applications in science, engineering, and data science. The syllabus progresses from foundational concepts of linearity and systems of linear equations (Unit I-II), through the abstract theory of vector spaces, linear transformations, and orthogonality (Unit III), to the practical applications of eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and SVD in machine learning and information retrieval (Units IV-V). Unit VI integrates all concepts through diverse real-world applications including traffic systems, circuit analysis, data compression, PageRank, and genetics modeling. With 45 contact hours distributed across 6 units, the course balances theoretical rigor with computational skills, emphasizing geometric intuition alongside algebraic manipulation. Students develop proficiency in mathematical modeling, developing their ability to formulate and solve complex problems in computer science, data analytics, and deep learning as evidenced by the course outcomes. Worked examples, computational implementations, and applications to modern technologies provide context and motivation throughout the curriculum.
